recipes.title: Classic Cheesecake 🍰

ingredients.name: cream cheese, softened to room temperature (910g)
large eggs, room temperature, lightly beaten

steps: Preheat oven to 325°F (160°C).
Make the crust first: combine the graham cracker crumbs, sugar and brown sugar and stir well. Add the melted butter and use a fork to combine everything well.
Pour the crumbs into a 9" springform pan and press firmly into the bottom and up the sides of the pan. Set aside.
In the bowl of a stand mixer (or a large bowl with a hand mixer), stir the cream cheese until smooth and creamy — don't over-beat or you'll incorporate too much air.
Add the sugar and stir again until creamy.
Add the sour cream, vanilla extract and salt and stir until well combined. Pause periodically to scrape the sides and bottom of the bowl with a spatula so everything is evenly incorporated.
With the mixer on low, gradually add the lightly beaten eggs one at a time, stirring just until each egg is incorporated. Scrape the bowl once more and make sure it's all well combined.
Pour the batter into the prepared springform pan. To insure against leaks, set the pan on a foil-lined cookie sheet.

Bake on the center rack at 325°F (160°C) for 50–60 minutes (or longer as needed). The edges will have puffed slightly and may be just turning light golden; the center should spring back to the touch but still be Jello-jiggly. Don't over-bake or the texture will suffer.

Remove from the oven and let cool on top of the oven for 10 minutes. Then run a knife around the inside of the pan to gently loosen the crust — this helps prevent cracks as it cools and shrinks. Leave the springform ring on.
Cool another 1–2 hours until near room temperature, then refrigerate overnight (or at least 6 hours). Remove the ring just before serving and return it to the pan to store. Enjoy!
recipes.notes: Cream cheese must be truly room temperature for a smooth batter. If the center is still very liquid after 60 min, keep going in 5-min checks — ovens vary 💕

recipes.title: Dubai Chocolate Bars 🍫🌰

ingredients.name: milk (or dark) chocolate, chopped or callets (340g)
white chocolate, melted (optional, for the drizzle)
green & gold food coloring (optional, for the drizzle)

steps: Optional decoration: mix the melted white chocolate with a drop of green (and/or gold) coloring and flick or drizzle it inside two chocolate bar molds. Let set a few minutes.

Melt the milk chocolate gently (short microwave bursts, stirring in between, or over a double boiler) until smooth. Spoon a thin layer into the molds and use the back of a spoon or a brush to coat the bottom and all the sides. Chill 10–15 minutes until set, then add a second thin coat if any spots look thin. Keep the remaining chocolate warm.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped kataifi and toast, stirring constantly, for 8–10 minutes until deeply golden and crisp all over.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the pistachio cream, tahini and salt until every strand is coated. Let cool for a few minutes so it doesn't melt the shell.
Spoon the pistachio filling into the set chocolate shells and press it in gently, leaving a little room at the top and keeping it off the rim.
Re-warm the reserved chocolate if needed and pour it over the filling, spreading to the edges to seal. Tap the mold on the counter to level it.
Chill for at least 1 hour until fully set, then pop the bars out of the molds. Store in the fridge or a cool spot and serve at room temperature for the best snap.
recipes.notes: Written from the classic viral version — pistachio cream and kataifi are the two must-haves (look for them at a Middle Eastern grocer). No molds? Line a loaf pan with parchment and build it in layers, then cut into bars 🌰

recipes.title: Patates Oturtması with Şehriye Pilavı 🍅🥔
steps: Prep the potatoes: slice them into thin-ish rounds, around ¼ inch. Toss with olive oil and salt, spread over baking sheets, and roast at 425°F for 25–30 minutes, flipping halfway. They should be partially cooked and lightly browned, not falling apart.
Make the beef sauce: in a large pot, sauté the diced onions in olive oil for about 7–8 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook another minute.
Add the ground beef and brown it thoroughly, breaking it into small pieces.
Stir in the tomato paste, biber salçası, crushed tomatoes, broth/water, paprika, pul biber, cumin, salt and pepper. Simmer 15–20 minutes — you want the sauce thick and rich, not watery.

Layer in a baking dish or pot: potatoes → beef → potatoes → beef → potatoes. Distribute the beef evenly so there's meat throughout instead of one giant meat layer. Pour some of the tomato sauce around the edges and over the top. Cover with foil.
Bake at 375°F for 40 minutes covered, then uncover and bake another 15–20 minutes until the potatoes are completely tender and the top is browned. Let rest 10–15 minutes before serving.

Şehriye pilavı: rinse the rice until the water runs clear and drain. Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot and toast the şehriye, stirring, until golden. Add the rice and stir 1–2 minutes to coat, then add the broth and salt. Bring to a boil, cover, and simmer on low 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Rest off the heat, covered, 10 minutes, then fluff.
Serve the oturtma over the pilav with a big spoonful of yogurt, fresh parsley, and extra pul biber on top.
recipes.notes: Big-batch recipe — roasting the potatoes instead of frying saves a ton of time. The pilav method was added from the ingredient list 🍚

recipes.title: Salçalı Köfte 🍅🧆
steps: Make the köfte mixture: grate the onion and squeeze out some of the excess liquid. Combine the ground beef, grated onion, garlic, egg, breadcrumbs, parsley, salt, black pepper, cumin, paprika and pul biber. Knead everything together with your hands for 3–4 minutes.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Shape the mixture into approximately 20–24 small oval patties. Keep them relatively thin so they cook evenly.
Brown: heat a little olive oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven. Brown the köfte in batches for 1–2 minutes per side — you are NOT trying to cook them through yet. Remove and set aside.

Make the sauce in the SAME pan to keep all the browned-beef flavor. Add butter/oil if needed. Cook the diced onion 3–4 minutes, add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, then add the tomato paste and cook 1–2 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes, 1 cup beef broth, paprika, cumin, pul biber, salt and black pepper. Stir and bring to a gentle simmer.
Return all the browned köfte to the sauce and spoon sauce over them. Cover and simmer on LOW for 20–25 minutes, gently turning them once. Köfte should reach 160°F internally.
If the sauce is too thin, remove the lid and simmer another 5–10 minutes; if it's too thick, add another splash of beef broth. You WANT plenty of sauce — it gets spooned over the pilav.
recipes.notes: Makes about 20–24 köfte. Serve over şehriye pilavı (see the Patates Oturtması recipe) with yogurt on the side 🍚

recipes.title: Fudgy Brownies 🍫

ingredients.name: cooking oil (olive or coconut oil are fine)
chocolate chunks or chips for the top (optional)

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Lightly grease an 8-inch square pan with cooking oil spray and line with parchment paper; set aside.
Combine the hot melted butter, oil and sugar in a medium bowl. Whisk well for about a minute.
Add the eggs and vanilla; beat until lighter in color (another minute).
Sift in the flour, cocoa powder and salt. Gently fold the dry ingredients into the wet until JUST combined — do NOT overbeat or it will affect the texture.
Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top out evenly. Optional: top with chocolate chunks or chips.

Bake for 20–25 minutes, or until the center no longer jiggles and is just set to the touch. For a fudgy center, a toothpick should come out dirty — the brownies keep baking in the hot pan once out of the oven!
Let cool to room temperature before slicing into 16 brownies.
recipes.notes: Optional add-ins: crushed walnuts, peanuts, almonds, pecans, white chocolate chips, peanut butter chips, chocolate chunks, or dried fruit (cranberries, raisins) — fold in the same way as the toppings 🍫

recipes.title: Steak Fries with Green Peppercorn Sauce 🥩🍟
steps: Pat the sirloin steaks dry and season generously with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

Heat the oil in a pan over high heat and sear the steaks 2–3 min per side. Add the butter, crushed garlic, thyme and rosemary, and spoon the foaming butter over the steaks for another minute. Rest for 5 min before slicing.
For the sauce, soften the finely chopped shallot in the same pan. Pour in the white wine and let it reduce by half.
Stir in the cream, green peppercorns, beef stock concentrate, soy sauce, mustard and salt. Simmer, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Cut the baking potatoes into fries and fry in hot oil until deep golden and crisp. Drain on paper towel.
Toss the hot fries with the chopped parsley, grated Parmesan, grated garlic and a pinch of salt.
Serve the sliced steak with the fries and spoon the green peppercorn sauce over the top.
recipes.notes: Method added from the ingredient list — tweak the timings to how you like your steak 💕

recipes.title: Banana Chocolate Chip Muffins 🍌🧁

ingredients.name: sour cream or whole milk Greek yogurt, room temp (60g)
semi-sweet chocolate chips (250g), + more for topping

steps: In a mixing bowl, roughly mash the bananas. Add the brown sugar and granulated sugar and mix well to combine.
Crack in the egg and mix for 2–3 min until the mixture turns a light, pale color.
Add the melted butter, vanilla bean paste and sour cream, and mix until well combined and blended.
In a separate bowl, mix the dry ingredients: flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt and cinnamon.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet batter and gently fold in. Add the chocolate chips and fold just to combine — do not over mix.
Let the batter sit at room temperature for 1 hour, undisturbed, before baking.
Scoop into a lined muffin tin, top with extra chocolate chips, and bake until a toothpick comes out clean (about 18–22 min at 350°F / 375°F for taller tops).
recipes.notes: The original recipe didn't give a bake time/temp — 350–375°F for ~18–22 min is a safe starting point. Resting the batter 1 hr makes them extra tender 🧁

recipes.title: Banana Bread

ingredients.name: unsalted butter (8 Tbsp), at room temperature

steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease and flour a bread loaf pan (9.25 long x 5.25 wide x 2.75 deep).
Lightly roast walnuts on a skillet, continuously stirring so they won't burn. Coarsely chop and cool to room temperature.
In a mixing bowl, cream together the softened butter and sugar (or honey if using honey).
Mash bananas with a fork until the consistency of chunky applesauce and add them to the batter along with the eggs, mixing until blended.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda and salt, then add to the batter.
Add the vanilla extract and mix in the chopped walnuts and chocolate chips. Pour into the prepared loaf pan.
Bake at 350°F for 55–60 min, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Let the banana bread rest for 10 min before transferring to a wire rack to cool.
recipes.notes: Prep 10 min, bake ~1 hour. The sugar can be swapped for honey 🍯

recipes.title: Arsenio's Crunch Cookie 🍪
steps: Mix soft butter, sugar, brown sugar, and salt.
Add eggs + vanilla, mix until smooth.
Fold in flour + baking soda until just combined.
Add chocolate chips.
Scoop onto a baking tray — makes 6 massive cookies.
Bake at 350°F for 12 minutes.
recipes.notes: the trick: spin them with a bowl or cup right out of the oven to shape… then let them rest 😮‍🔥

diary.note: The taste was a 10/10 but the baking time needed more. It was still pretty soft and raw in the middle. We should divide it into 4 minimum next time.
